TO THE HONORABLE PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION OF TEXAS AND MUNICIPAL
REGULATORY AUTHORITIES:

       COMES NOW EL PASO ELECTRIC COMPANY (“EPE” and “Company”) in the above-
styled cause, and files this application for approval of a new tariff applicable to very large, high
load factor customers. EPE proposes to create Schedule No. 27 – High Load Factor Large Power
Service Rate (HLFLP) and requests that the aforementioned schedule be made effective on May
12, 2026, which is 35 days from the filing of this application on April 7, 2026. The rates reflected
in the proposed tariff were previously approved by the Public Utility Commission of Texas
(“Commission”) on July 31, 2025, in Docket No. 56903.

                                 II.   PARTIES AND JURISDICTION

         EPE is an electric utility, a public utility, and a utility, as those terms are defined in the
Public Utility Regulatory Act, Tex. Util. Code Ann. §§ 11.004(1) and 31.002(6) (PURA). EPE is
headquartered in El Paso, Texas, with its business address located at 100 N. Stanton Street,
El Paso, Texas 79901, and provides services to customers in both Texas and New Mexico. This
application presents a new retail rate offering and will not affect the rates or fuel factor of other
customers.

         The Commission has jurisdiction over this matter under PURA §§ 14.001 (general powers),
32.001 (original jurisdiction over rates, operations, and services), and 36.101 through 36.111
(procedures for utility-proposed rate changes). The municipalities that also have jurisdiction over
this matter because they have retained original jurisdiction over EPE’s retail rates are Anthony,
Clint, El Paso, Horizon City, San Elizario, Socorro, Van Horn, and Vinton. EPE is
contemporaneously filing this application with each of these municipal regulatory authorities.

                        III. TESTIMONY AND SUPPORTING EXHIBITS

         Included in this application are direct testimony and exhibits supporting approval of the
new tariffs, as well as the related Energy Service Agreement (ESA) for informational purposes.
EPE offers the direct testimony of James Schichtl in support of this application.

         James Schichtl is EPE’s Vice President of Customer and Regulatory Strategy. Mr. Schichtl
describes in detail EPE’s proposed tariff for retail service to new qualifying large customers
(Exhibit JS-1).1

         In addition, EPE includes in its application, for informational purposes only, the ESA
required for service under the new tariff (Exhibit JS-2).

     IV. ELIGIBILITY FOR THE HIGH LOAD FACTOR LARGE POWER SERVICE
                                                     RATE

        The proposed Schedule No. 27 – High Load Factor Large Power Service Rate (HLFLP) is
intended for service to very large data center or advanced manufacturing customers in EPE’s Texas
service territory. To be eligible for service under the new tariff, Customers must have an annual
peak demand of 75 MW or larger and an annual load factor of at least 85%. Recently, EPE has
been fielding and analyzing potential loads for a variety of inquiries that are primarily categorized
as data centers. Wurldwide LLC is currently constructing a major Data Center operation in
northeast El Paso, near EPE’s Newman Power Station. Once fully operational, the Wurldwide
Data Center is expected to operate with a peak demand of 1,000 MW (1 GW) and an annual load
factor over 90% and would qualify for service under the new tariff.

        EPE’s existing Schedule No. 25 – Large Power Service Rate is technically applicable for
retail service for these types of customers. EPE is proposing the new tariff and rates to reflect the
significant operational and, by extension, cost of service differences between these very large,
high-load factor customers and the existing Large Power rate class.

                       V.       DESIGN OF RATES FOR RETAIL SERVICE

        The proposed Schedule No. 27 – High Load Factor Large Power Service Rate (HLFLP)
includes rates that have been previously approved by the Commission as Rate Schedule 33A and
reflect a cost-of-service analysis of the estimated load profile for a large data center.2 The rates
are designed to fully recover the expected cost of power supplied. Service under the new retail
rate schedule requires that the customer enter into an ESA with the Company. EPE also requests
that Rate Schedule 33A be terminated upon approval of Rate Schedule 27 in that Rate Schedule
33A will no longer be needed.

        The new tariff will allow customers to participate under the Green Energy Plus (GEP)
Tariff, which is applicable for customers in Texas.3 The GEP allows eligible customers to enter
into procurement agreements with EPE to supply a portion or all of their annual energy

                              V.     NOTICE REQUIREMENTS

        The proposed tariff is a new rate offering for designated customers and no other customers’
rates will be increased or decreased as a result of approval of EPE’s application. Consequently,
the notice requirements of 16 Tex. Admin. Code (TAC) §22.51 are not applicable. Pursuant to 16
TAC §22.55, EPE proposes that notice be given to Anthony, Clint, El Paso, Horizon City, San
Elizario, Socorro, Van Horn, and Vinton, the municipalities retaining original jurisdiction over
EPE’s rates, by service of a copy of the application and by a one-time publication in newspapers
in general circulation in EPE’s service territory. A copy of the draft notice for publication is
attached as Exhibit B.

                                         VII. PRAYER

Commission issue an order approving EPE’s proposed Schedule No. 27 – High Load Factor Large
Power Service Rate and terminating Rate Schedule 33A and such other relief as EPE has shown
is justified.

                            NOTICE OF NEW RATE REQUEST

       On April 7, 2026, El Paso Electric Company (“EPE” or the “Company”) filed an
application (“Application”) with the Public Utility Commission of Texas (“Commission”) for
approval of a High Load Factor Large Power (HLFLP) tariff for qualifying customers in Texas.
EPE’s Application was assigned Docket No. _____and is styled Application of El Paso Electric
Company for a High Load Factor Large Power Service Tariff. EPE also filed the Application
simultaneously with El Paso, Anthony, Clint, Horizon City, San Elizario, Socorro, Van Horn, and
Vinton as the municipal regulatory authorities.
         The proposed tariff is Schedule No. 27-High Load Factor Large Power Service Rate and is
applicable to customers with expected peak demand of 70 MW or greater, and a load factor of 85%
or greater. The rates reflected in the new tariff were previously approved by the Commission on
July 31, 2025, in Docket No. 56903. The tariff also allows participation on the Green Energy Plus
tariff (GEP), which allows eligible customers to enter into procurement agreements for the supply
of a portion or all of their annual energy requirements from renewable resources.
        EPE is asking the Commission to make the proposed tariffs effective by May 12, 2026,
which is 35 days from the date the Application was filed. Persons with questions or who want
more information about EPE's Application may contact EPE at 100 N. Stanton Street, El Paso,
Texas 79901, or call (915) 543-5970, during normal business hours. Persons may also email
customercare@epelectric.com with questions or to request more information or a copy of the
Application. A complete copy of the Application is available for inspection at the address listed
above. The Commission will review EPE's Application, establish an intervention date for
interested persons, and determine whether EPE's Application should be approved. The
Commission's proceeding to review EPE's Application has been assigned Docket No. ____.
        Persons who wish to intervene in or comment upon these proceedings, or obtain further

intervene their email addresses, or other information that can provide to the Commission a means
of electronic service Hearing- and speech-impaired individuals may contact the commission

18                III.   EPE’s Need for the High Load Factor Large Power Tariff
19   Q13.   WHY IS EPE FILING THE NEW LARGE POWER TARIFF AT THIS TIME?
20   A.     Rate Schedules 33A and 33B were approved by the Commission on July 31, 2025, for
21          service to Wurldwide LLC, a future data center now under construction in northeast

22              capacity requirements of these customers also necessitate tariff terms and conditions
23              and contractual commitments that are not typically required of large customers.

 7   Q23.   PLEASE DESCRIBE THE ENERGY SERVICE AGREEMENT REQUIRED
 8          BETWEEN EPE AND CUSTOMER FOR SERVICE UNDER SCHEDULE HLFLP.

10          for service to large, high-load factor customers whose power requirements may require
11          significant investment by EPE. The contract term, minimum payments, and security
12          provisions are designed to ensure that other customers and EPE are protected from
13          early termination or significant reductions to contracted demand. Because EPE expects
14          there may be significantly different characteristics between customers who qualify for
15          the HLFLP tariff, the ESA provides the flexibility to establish service and contract
16          terms to address the unique nature of these customers while also protecting the system.

23          requirements for service and customer protection.

25   Q25.   HOW DO THE TARIFF AND ESA PROTECT EPE’S EXISTING CUSTOMERS?
26   A.     The rates reflected in the HLFLP tariff are cost-based and reflect cost allocation under
27          standard cost causation principles. Future updates for these rates will follow the same
28          ratemaking protocols as with all other retail tariffs. This protects other customer classes
29          from cross-subsidization of authorized annual costs.
30                 The tariff and supporting ESA also include provisions designed to protect other
31          customer classes from financial exposure to the incremental cost to provide service to

  1          the very large customers eligible for service under the HLFLP tariff. These include a
 2          minimum contract term, damages for termination of the contract for service within the
 3          Initial Term, and security requirements. The proposed tariff sets out how required

 5          the security is adjusted over the term of the service agreement. The tariff also specifies
 6          allowed forms of security to be provided by the Customer if required. These include
 7          cash or cash equivalents, letters of credit, or parental guarantee.

10   A.     As I noted previously, providing service to the size of the customer contemplated for
